root_cause: The test_export_model_precommit test for the OPT-GPTQ quantized model (katuni4ka/opt-125m-gptq) fails because the inference outputs produced by the exported OpenVINO model differ from the reference PyTorch framework outputs beyond the acceptable tolerance. The commit being tested (GPU clang-tidy nullptr modernization, PR #37029) changes the GPU plugin only; however this PyTorch LLM test runs on CPU. The accuracy divergence may be a pre-existing flaky test (quantized model accuracy can vary across runs, or model weights may have changed on HuggingFace Hub) OR may indicate a regression introduced in CPU kernel paths indirectly affected by the PR. The model is loaded from an external HuggingFace Hub source (katuni4ka/opt-125m-gptq) and quantized via GPT-Q, making it sensitive to library version changes in transformers (5.5.3) and auto-gptq (6.0.3) detected in the test output.
recommended_actions: Check whether this test has failed for other recent PRs unrelated to GPU changes — if so this is a flaky/model-version issue.
Inspect if transformers==5.5.3 or auto-gptq==6.0.3 changed the quantized model's default generation, which could shift accuracy.
If the test is consistently failing for GPU-only PRs, add it to the known-flaky or skip list for GPU-only changes.
Re-run the test to confirm whether the failure is intermittent.
prevention_strategies: For quantized model hub tests that depend on external model weights and third-party quantization libraries, pin exact versions and consider caching model weights to avoid drift. Tag these tests as potentially flaky when the PR does not touch the relevant compute path.
historical_context: First occurrence of this exact signature in CI Doctor MQ records. GPU clang-tidy PRs should not affect CPU inference accuracy; if this test fails again in future GPU PRs it should be treated as a flaky test.
